title: [P2.10a-hardening-c-pre] Server-authored transport-origin fact: stamp at every command ingress, thread through dispatch into the Gate-1 BearerSessionWitness
description:
PREREQUISITE FILED BY THE ARCHITECT per governor ruling comment-9431831c on task-ffa05408a22b4456b4594b3c06d1206d (the FENCE arm): the stage-E bearer fence is unimplementable today because BearerSessionWitness carries only {sessionId} — daemon-command-registry.ts:303 constructs it as {sessionId: principal.principalId} — so a browser call and an MCP call presenting the SAME paired HUMAN session are byte-for-byte indistinguishable at authorizeBearerPresentation, and any transport allowlist there is decorative (worker-2a834a38's structural finding, comment-b8b220e3, accepted in full by the governor).

DELIVER: a SERVER-AUTHORED transport-origin fact, stamped at each ingress call site and threaded to the witness — never caller-asserted, never read from the wire, headers, payload or env of the REQUEST (same admission principle as ruling (A) on task-2f554e29: the server knows which entry it is).

MEASURED THREAD PATH at HEAD (18b1493d-era): the ONLY command entries are `handleCommandRequest` / `handleAsyncCommandRequest` (apps/daemon/src/http/http-adapter.ts:128/:156-era) -> `dispatch` -> the registry composition (daemon-command-registry.ts) whose productContractGate1 branch builds the witness at :303. Ingress callers of the two entries, each knowing its own transport as a compile-time literal: apps/daemon/src/http/http-command-ingress.ts (HTTP listener), apps/daemon/src/mcp-dispatch-port.ts (MCP stdio), apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.ts (MCP HTTP), apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts, apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/demo-seed-main.ts.

DESIGN (binding): a frozen TRANSPORT_ORIGIN roster (e.g. HTTP_LISTENER / MCP_STDIO / MCP_HTTP / AGENT_WRAPPER / DEMO_SEED — exact spellings the worker fixes to house style) declared beside the adapter contract; the two entry functions gain a REQUIRED third parameter `origin` (a roster member) so EVERY caller is compile-forced to stamp its literal — required-param completeness IS the bidirectional guarantee; dispatch threads it beside `principal`; the CommandHandler contract is UNTOUCHED (origin reaches only the registry-internal composition); the gate-1 branch widens the witness to Object.freeze({ sessionId, transportOrigin: origin }). No caller can present an origin: the parameter exists only in server modules, and an arm proves a wire field named transportOrigin (header/payload) never reaches the witness.

CONSUMER: task-ffa05408 (the fence: bearer permitted iff transportOrigin is a named non-browser survivor; browser-origin bearer refused with its own code+layer; bidirectional arms become non-vacuous because the origin fact separates the populations). Registered in that row's dependsOn.

The frozen TRANSPORT_ORIGIN roster exists beside the adapter contract with an exact-membership arm (bidirectional set-equality against the stamped call sites — enumerate the served side from the CALLERS, not the roster constant); the two entry functions require the origin parameter (compile-time: a caller omitting it fails typecheck — prove by the planted-error control) and each of the five callers stamps ITS OWN literal, quoted per call site.

BearerSessionWitness carries transportOrigin authored ONLY at the entry parameter: an arm drives a command through the production HTTP ingress and asserts the witness the gate-1 handler received carries HTTP_LISTENER; an MCP-dispatch-port arm asserts MCP_STDIO; a request carrying a transportOrigin header AND a transportOrigin payload field changes NEITHER (the wire cannot reach the fact — assert byte-equality of the witness against the stamped literal).

The CommandHandler contract and every non-gate-1 handler are UNTOUCHED (`git diff --stat` limited to the owned roster; no handler signature change); authorizeBearerPresentation and the bearer refusal roster are NOT edited here — the fence itself is task-ffa05408's.

Mutation drills with restore proofs (git diff for tracked paths): re-stamp one caller with another transport's literal -> that transport's witness arm reds; derive origin from a request field instead of the parameter -> the wire-cannot-reach arm reds; drop the origin from the witness construction -> the gate-1 witness arms red. Gates standalone/unpiped with counts: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` (quote `$ tsc`), the adapter/registry/ingress/mcp suites from apps/daemon via `pnpm exec vitest run --root . --config package.json <files>`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` path-attributed with foreign red disclosed verbatim; every production source <= 250 lines except pre-existing over-cap files which must not grow materially (daemon-command-registry.ts is 346 — the edit is a handful of lines; if it crosses 400 split by subtraction); explicit-pathspec commit; completion comment names task-ffa05408 as consumer and the governor ruling comment-9431831c.

Required parameter, not optional: compile-time completeness across all callers is the point; no default value anywhere.
CommandHandler contract untouched; the fact reaches only the registry-internal gate-1 composition; the bearer fence itself belongs to task-ffa05408.
Explicit-pathspec commits; foreign WIP preserved; <=250 lines per new production source; TDD red-first through the production entries.

=== THE GAP IS REAL (DoD 1 premises hold) ===
- `git grep -n 'sessionId: principal.principalId' HEAD -- apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts` EXIT 0 -> :304 (description says :303; one line of drift). Witness is `Object.freeze({ sessionId: principal.principalId })`, sessionId-only.
- `git grep -q transportOrigin HEAD` EXIT 1 repo-wide, and EXIT 1 under apps/daemon/src. Nothing to adopt; no duplicate.
- Both prerequisite rows DONE (dependsOnUnmet is empty).

=== THE DESCRIPTION'S THREAD PATH IS WRONG IN FOUR PLACES ===
Measured PRODUCTION ingress callers are FOUR, not five:
1. apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener.ts:273 (handleAsyncCommandRequest)
2. apps/daemon/src/mcp-dispatch-port.ts:183 (handleAsyncCommandRequest)
3. apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts:178 (handleCommandRequest)
4. apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-verifier.ts:127 (handleCommandRequest) <- NOT IN THE DESCRIPTION'S ROSTER

Named but NOT callers:
- apps/daemon/src/http/http-command-ingress.ts EXISTS but is the shared ingress-ORDER module (exports `authenticateHttpRequest`, `prepareCommand`, `PreparedCommand`, `HttpAccessResult`) that BOTH entries call INTO. It makes zero calls to either entry. It is one layer below the transport boundary and knows no transport.
- apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.ts: comment mention at :22 only, zero calls.
- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/demo-seed-main.ts: `git grep -c` EXIT 1, zero references.

=== THE BLOCKER: A REQUIRED THIRD PARAMETER REACHES 32 FILES, THE CAP IS 10 ===
`git grep -l 'handleCommandRequest(\|handleAsyncCommandRequest(' HEAD -- apps adapters packages | wc -l` -> **32**.
Both entries are 2-arity today (http-adapter.ts:128 and :156, each `(deps, request)`). Adding a REQUIRED third parameter is a TS arity error at every one of those 32 files: 4 production callers, 3 runtime-tier fixture modules (goals/goal-closure-test-fixtures.ts, journal/journal-test-harness.ts, planning/expansion-release-selector-test-fixtures.ts) and 24 test files, plus the definition site.
Add two more the shape-grep finds: apps/daemon/src/index.ts:105 re-exports `handleCommandRequest` on the daemon's PUBLIC barrel, and apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts:576 asserts `expectTypeOf<Parameters<typeof daemon.handleCommandRequest>>()` — an export-surface scanner that moves with the arity.

That is ~34 distinct affectedFiles. `submit_plan` HARD-REJECTS above 10. Epic rail 8(A) forbids the alternative outright: "do not ship a narrow roster and let a worker discover the rest."

No design avoids this. Origin cannot ride on `CommandAdapterDeps` (one daemon serves HTTP and MCP concurrently, so a deps-level fact cannot vary per request), and putting it on `HttpCommandRequest` breaks the same 32 literal constructions. A second entry pair carrying the origin would leave the old 2-arity pair importable, which is exactly the "decorative allowlist" weakness this row exists to close.

=== PROPOSED SLICING (governor call — needs a DoD 2 amendment either way) ===
Each row compiles; the end state satisfies task rail 2 exactly, and there is never a permissive window.
- **A (this row, DoD 2 amended):** frozen TRANSPORT_ORIGIN roster beside the adapter contract; third parameter added as OPTIONAL at the type level; threaded through `dispatch` into the gate-1 witness; all FOUR production callers stamp their own literal; the gate-1 composition REFUSES fail-closed with its own code+layer when the origin is absent or not a roster member — a refusal, not a default, so rail 1 and epic rail 4 both hold from day one. Plus the wire-cannot-reach arm and the HTTP_LISTENER/MCP_STDIO witness arms. ~9 files. Delivers the security fact and is production-reachable immediately.
- **B:** stamp the ~27 test/fixture call sites (mechanical; splits cleanly by directory if it must).
- **C:** tighten the parameter to REQUIRED and update index-surface.test.ts's `Parameters` assertion. Small. This row is what delivers rail 2's compile-time completeness and the planted-error control DoD 2 names.

RECOMMENDED: take A now — it closes the actual security hole that task-ffa05408's fence waits on, because an absent origin refuses rather than permits. B and C are then mechanical and carry no security risk.

The single alternative is one cap-excepted ~34-file row. I am not narrowing the roster to fit, and I am not planning against a DoD clause I have measured to be unsatisfiable inside the cap.
